gen_risks.description: ADISA and MIPA lack prior experience in managing large donor-funded projects, creating high operational, financial management, and procurement implementation risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) within ADISA staffed with qualified finance and procurement specialists, initially supported by CFCU in MoF.
gen_risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations

gen_risks.description: Legacy paper registers, missing national ID numbers, and lack of basic IT infrastructure across multiple agencies impede back-end digitization and system interoperability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phased rollout of new IT systems, targeted digitization of legacy archives, and mandatory integration of agency databases with the national interoperability platform.
gen_risks.evidence: Seven institutions encompassed by the proposed project have no IT system in place. Entire business processes are performed manually

gen_risks.description: Manual and unintegrated payroll systems across participating budgetary and non-budgetary agencies expose the project to substantial financial management and control risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure dedicated project financial management software, enforce a detailed Financial Management Manual, and support HRMIS implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: payroll systems remain by and large manual systems, and the associated controls are manually based as well.

gen_risks.description: Resistance from line agencies and civil servants to ceding front-office authority to ADISA/CSC, alongside potential delays in passing required omnibus reform legislation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a structured change management and communications campaign overseen directly by the Prime Minister-chaired Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts

gen_risks.description: The ambitious and compressed reform timeline risks schedule slippage in completing business process re-engineering and establishing the central Citizen Service Center.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure performance incentives via Results-Based Financing (DLIs) and deploy Project Preparation Facility (PPF) funds for rapid start-up execution.
gen_risks.evidence: The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk, which is mitigated by the project's span and incentives to deliver up to 2020.

gen_risks.description: Over-emphasis on digital e-services and high-end urban CSCs risks diminishing service access for poor, rural, elderly, and vulnerable populations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain local physical service windows, establish assisted digital access points, deploy call centers, and deliver targeted non-digital information outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

gen_risks.description: Civil works for constructing the new Citizen Service Center building in Tirana pose localized noise, dust, waste, and worker safety environmental risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate World Bank Category B Environmental Management Plan (EMP) requirements directly into civil works bidding and construction contracts with PMU oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site

gen_risks.description: Complex inter-sectoral coordination requirements across more than a dozen participating ministries and agencies create operational decision-making bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the Prime Minister's Delivery Unit (DU) and weekly Steering Committee meetings to manage inter-agency collaboration and resolve operational roadblocks.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: Lack of specialized technical ICT skills within government authorities to design, optimize, and implement complex software architecture and database interoperability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate USD 5 million in Technical Assistance funding to hire specialized international and local ICT advisors to support NAIS and ADISA.
gen_risks.evidence: the authorities do not have staff with the technical skills and experience needed to implement the reform process.

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve agreed Disbursement Linked Indicators or complete prerequisite DLI#5 will result in the withholding of RBF loan disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize early completion of the Reform Policy Document and PDO baseline survey (DLI#5), supported by targeted PPF and TA resources.
gen_risks.evidence: No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved.

gen_risks.description: Modest national internet penetration (60%) and lower digital literacy among older and rural citizens constrain adoption of online e-Albania services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish assisted digital access outreach networks in local government offices and internet cafes, supported by multi-channel information platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: modest levels of internet penetration at only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013 (WDI).

gen_risks.description: Future fiscal constraints may lead to inadequate funding for post-project IT system operation, software maintenance, license fees, and periodic technological upgrades.
gen_risks.mitigation: Capture government cost savings from business process re-engineering and incremental revenue gains from increased service efficiency to finance ongoing O&M.
gen_risks.evidence: Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance. To continue efficiency improvements... Government will have to upgrade periodically.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
